Using the Widget API

The Widget API lets you create, list and delete widgets from any language. It is a plain REST interface that speaks JSON, and every request needs an API key sent in the Authorization header.

Creating a widget

Send a POST request to /v1/widgets with a JSON body. The service answers with the new widget and its identifier, which you will need for later calls. Widget names must be unique inside a project, and they may contain letters, digits and dashes only.

const res = await fetch("https://api.example.com/v1/widgets", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${key}` },
  body: JSON.stringify({ name: "demo" }),
});
console.log(await res.json());

Limits

Each key may make a limited number of calls. The table below shows the defaults for every plan, and you can ask support to raise them when your traffic grows beyond what the plan allows.

PlanCalls per minuteWidgets
Free6010
Team6001,000
Scale6,000Unlimited

Errors

When something goes wrong the API answers with a 4xx or 5xx status and a JSON error object. Read the status page before you retry, because a retry storm only makes an outage longer for everybody who depends on the service.

  • 400: the body was not valid JSON.
  • 401: the key is missing or wrong.
  • 429: slow down and retry later.
